title: Data Clumps
pattern: Multiple independent functions consistently accepting the exact same cluster of 3-4 primitive arguments in their signatures, representing a cohesive domain concept.
why_bad: Structural redundancy and high risk of out-of-sync modifications. If the domain concept expands (e.g., adding a connection timeout parameter), every single function signature and call site must be updated in parallel. It indicates that a hidden struct is waiting to be extracted.
detection: Look for identical groupings of 3+ parameters of the same names and types appearing across multiple distinct function signatures.
counterexample: `Context-dependent`. Highly generic APIs or mathematics libraries where coordinates `(x, y, z)` are passed together but represent independent primitives with no shared domain behavior.
fix: Introduce a cohesive parameter struct that groups these variables into a single conceptual unit.
source: *Martin Fowler - Refactoring (1999)*, Chapter 3, "Data Clumps"; *Steve McConnell - Code Complete (2004)*, Chapter 13.
